questions.q: The decimal value of the binary number 111010 is:
Mail merge in MS Word is used to —
options: Merge two Word files into one
Join two tables side by side
Create many personalised documents from one template and a data list
questions.solution: **Mail merge** produces one finished copy per record — same letter body, different names and addresses.

questions.q: Downloading a large software file from the Internet should use —
questions.solution: A file must arrive complete and in order — **TCP's reliability** is worth its slowness.

questions.q: The default file extension of a workbook created in MS Excel 2019 is:
questions.solution: Excel 2007 onwards saves workbooks as .xlsx (Office Open XML). .xls is the 97-2003 format, .xlsm is macro-enabled, .ods is OpenDocument.
questions.shortcut: X = XML = 2007+ across all Office extensions.

questions.q:
Choose the best summary.

Vertical farms grow lettuce with a tenth of the water open fields need and no pesticide at all. But their LEDs and chillers gulp electricity, which is why the industry has clustered around leafy greens and left staples like wheat alone.
options: Vertical farming saves water but its power costs keep it to high-value crops.
Vertical farming will replace traditional agriculture.
Open-field farming wastes all its water.
questions.solution: Water saving + energy constraint + crop choice is the complete claim; option 1 states it. Option 2 overreaches, option 3 exaggerates, option 4 states an implication as fact too strongly.

questions.q: Select the correct passive form of the sentence: 'The principal awarded the topper a gold medal.'
options: A gold medal was awarded the topper by the principal.
The topper was awarded a gold medal by the principal.
The topper was awarding a gold medal by the principal.
A gold medal was awarded by the topper to the principal.
questions.solution: Promote the person: *The topper was awarded a gold medal by the principal.* The medal-promoted option is missing *to* before the topper; 'was awarding' is the wrong form after was; making the medal awarded by the topper reverses the ceremony.

questions.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

The price of these shoes / are too high / for a student / to afford.
questions.solution: The head noun is **price** (singular), so the error is the plural verb: 'are too high' should be 'is too high'.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct according to the passage?
options: The cooperative began with over two hundred households
The private trader paid more for milk with a higher fat content
Membership grew from twelve to over two hundred households in about four years
The members say the extra income is the biggest change
questions.solution: Paragraph 1 gives twelve households at the start; paragraph 3 says 'within four years the membership had grown to over two hundred'. The second option swaps the numbers; the third reverses the trader's 'fixed low price regardless of quality'; the fourth reverses 'the biggest change is not the extra income but the confidence'.
questions.shortcut: For number options, check both the before and after figure; swapped figures are the commonest trap.
questions.passage:
When the women of Rampur formed a milk cooperative, only twelve households joined. Each morning they brought their milk to a single shed, where it was measured, tested for fat and poured into a shared cooling tank. Before this, a private trader had collected milk from their doorsteps, paid a fixed low price regardless of quality, and often delayed payment for weeks.

The cooperative changed three things. Payment was now linked to the fat content, so families that fed their animals well earned more. Money was paid every ten days, directly into bank accounts opened in the women's own names. And because the milk was cooled at once, less of it turned sour on the way to the dairy.

Within four years the membership had grown to over two hundred households. The members say the biggest change is not the extra income but the confidence: women who once stayed silent at village meetings now keep the cooperative's accounts and argue with officials about prices.

questions.q: Which ocean is the **only one named after a country**?
questions.solution: The **Indian Ocean** takes its name from India; it is the third largest and the warmest ocean.

questions.q: **Meteors** ('shooting stars') mostly burn up in which layer of the atmosphere?
questions.solution: The **mesosphere** (up to 80-85 km) is dense enough to burn incoming meteors by friction - and it is also the coldest layer (about -90 degrees C).

questions.q: Coffee cultivation in India began in the Baba Budan hills, which lie in which state?
questions.solution: The **Baba Budan (Chandra Drona) hills** of Chikmagalur district, Karnataka, are the traditional home of Indian coffee - legend says seeds were brought from Yemen in the 17th century.

questions.q: Which subatomic particle carries a **negative** charge?
questions.solution: The **electron** (found by J.J. Thomson) is negatively charged; the proton is positive; the neutron has no charge.

questions.q: Two tables are sold at ₹960 each, one at a profit of x% and the other at a loss of x%. If the total loss is ₹80, x equals:
questions.shortcut: ₹80 is 4% of the CP — never of the SP (that would suggest x ≈ 4.1).

questions.q: From an external point $P$, a tangent $PT = 10$ cm and a secant $PAB$ are drawn to a circle. If $PA = 5$ cm, the length of the chord $AB$ (the internal part) is:
questions.solution:
$PT^2 = PA \times PB \Rightarrow 100 = 5 \times PB \Rightarrow PB = 20$ cm.

$AB = PB - PA = 20 - 5 = 15$ cm.
questions.shortcut: Whole secant $20$, so internal part $15$ cm. Trap: $20$ cm — that is $PB$, not $AB$.

questions.q: The curved surface area of a cylinder is $352$ sq cm and its height is $8$ cm. Its radius is (take $\pi = 22/7$):
A merchant sells at the cost price and gains $11\frac{1}{9}\%$ by cheating on the weight. How many grams does he give in place of one kilogram?
questions.shortcut: $11\frac{1}{9}\% = \frac{1}{9}$ — a ninth of what he gives, so 100 g on 900 g.

questions.q: Arrange as in a dictionary: **Judge, Judo, Joust, Journal, Jostle.** Which word is **second from the right**?
questions.solution: 2nd letters: o (Jostle, Journal, Joust) vs u (Judge, Judo); o < u → the o-group comes first. 3rd letters: s (Jostle) vs u (Journal, Joust) → Jostle first. 4th letters: r (Journal) vs s (Joust) → Journal, Joust. Full order: Jostle, Journal, Joust, Judge, Judo → slot 5 + 1 − 2 = 4 → **Judge**.
questions.shortcut: The 2nd letter splits J-o... before J-u... — check column two before assuming a shared stem.

questions.q:
**Statement:** The price of a notebook rose from ₹40 to ₹50, while the price of a pen rose from ₹10 to ₹15.

**Conclusions:**
I. The price of the notebook rose by a larger percentage than the price of the pen.
II. The price of the pen rose by 50%.

Which of the conclusions follow(s) from the statement?
questions.solution: Notebook: (50 − 40)/40 = 25%. Pen: (15 − 10)/10 = 50%. I claims 25% > 50% — false, **does not follow** (a bigger rupee rise is not a bigger percentage rise). II is exactly 50% — **follows**. Answer: **Only II**.
questions.shortcut: Compare percentages on the base, not the rupee jump.

questions.q: Two different positions of the same dice are shown. Which letter is on the face opposite to **I**? (Ignore the orientation of the letters/numbers.)

questions.solution: The two views share **H** and **J** — two common faces, so each of them touches the other faces shown. The face left over in the first view (**I**) and the face left over in the second (**L**) must therefore be opposite each other.
questions.shortcut: Two common faces in two views: the leftovers are opposite.

questions.q:
**Statement:** Advertisement: 'Fresh vegetables delivered to your door within 30 minutes — order on our app!'

**Assumptions:**
I. Some people want fresh vegetables delivered quickly.
II. Some people are able to place orders through a mobile app.

Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
options: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
questions.solution: Negate I: nobody wants quick delivery — the advert's hook is useless, so I is **implicit**. Negate II: nobody can order through an app — no one can respond, so II is **implicit**. Answer: **both**.
questions.shortcut: An advert assumes its hook attracts someone and that someone can respond.
